clue.text: Crafty move before close of play

indicators.note: the close of something is its very end, so only the final letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: to shift is to move
final letter of play

explanation.surface: A sly tactic in a game, played just before stumps are drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' places the move ahead of the single closing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shifty looks evasive and untrustworthy, which is close to sly or cunning.

clue.text: Surprise Mum with an unusual treat

indicators.note: an unusual version of something is out of its normal form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: 'mum' as in keep mum: the call for silence
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Springing an unexpected treat on your mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum looks like mother, but here it means silence, as in 'mum's the word'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter someone is to stun or shock them badly, a strong form of taking them aback.

clue.text: Perfect profession for a croupier?

blocks.note: first meaning: flawless, as good as can be
second meaning, read as two words: what a card dealer would declare about their job

explanation.surface: Asking whether running the gaming table is the dream job.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as I DEAL: a croupier deals the cards, and a profession is also a declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes something matching the highest standard, flawless in every respect.

clue.text: News of current interest?

blocks.note: surface reading: topical news, what is happening right now
setter's reading: current as in the flow of the sea, so news about the tide

explanation.walkthrough: TIDINGS sounds as if it contains tide, the sea's current, so the word is news about tides.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old word for reports or information brought to someone.

clue.text: Decorated about noon, has to deliver a speech

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other here

blocks.note: to orate is to make a formal speech
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Someone who got a medal around midday has to give a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Decorated suggests an honour, but it is the definition in the sense of adorned.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately adorned with ornament, a fair match for decorated.

clue.text: Take stock of others

blocks.note: surface reading: make an inventory or review of something
setter's reading: carry off someone else's livestock

explanation.walkthrough: Stock here is farm animals, and rustling is the theft of cattle or horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle, so the verb means stealing livestock belonging to someone else.

clue.text: Chilled port for Michael?

blocks.note: first meaning: the cold Russian harbour city on the White Sea
second meaning: Saint Michael, chief of the angels

explanation.surface: Asking what cold port wine a man called Michael might drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Port suggests the drink, but it is a harbour: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) in northern Russia, ice-bound in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is one of the chief angels in Christian tradition, given the title archangel.

clue.text: Cheer for most of the players at end of game

indicators.note: most of a word means a good part is kept and the tail is dropped
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: a team of players, as in football or cricket, is an eleven
taken as written
last letter of game

explanation.surface: Most of a team celebrating when the match finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheer looks like a shout but is the verb meaning to lift someone's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone's mood is to raise their spirits, which is what cheering them does.

clue.text: Screw on the doors inside

blocks.note: surface reading: a DIY instruction to fix a screw to interior doors
setter's reading: screw is British slang for a jail guard who controls the doors of those inside

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a screw is a jail warder, and 'inside' means in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw is slang for a warder, the official guarding inmates and keeping the cells locked.

clue.text: Take a sea voyage - relax!

indicators.note: take tells the solver to lift a run of letters straight out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the run starts at the last letter of the first word and stops inside the third

explanation.surface: Advice to go on a cruise and unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voyage' looks like an anagram signal, but shuffling 'a sea' gives two As; the letters sit in a row across 'Take a sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to slacken or take things more gently, much like relaxing.

clue.text: Private matter that never comes to light

definitions.text: Private matter that never comes to light

blocks.note: surface reading: a personal affair kept to oneself
setter's reading: something kept in the dark, unlit as well as undisclosed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes to light' means becomes known, and something dark is literally never lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark secret is a shameful hidden fact that someone keeps concealed from everyone.

clue.text: Somehow lost on points - or was robbed?

definitions.note: the answer is the past participle too: was stolen

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged in an unspecified new order

blocks.note: taken as written
two compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A boxer losing a points decision and feeling cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost on points' suggests boxing; the points are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Something robbed has been taken unlawfully, which is exactly what stolen goods are.

clue.text: Sailor on a voyage to save money

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced seaman
someone travelling is away from home

explanation.surface: A seaman going on a trip to put cash aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To salt something away is to store it secretly for the future, especially savings.

clue.text: He leaves new chain stores with pastry

indicators.note: when something leaves it departs, so those letters are taken out
new suggests a fresh version, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walks out of a newly opened supermarket carrying a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H and E from chain stores, then rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a crescent-shaped flaky French bread roll, a kind of pastry.

clue.text: Drew attention to article pocketed by accused

indicators.note: something pocketed is put inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to be indicted is to be formally charged
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece highlighted that money was taken by the defendant.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to point it out, directing others' notice towards it.

clue.text: Illness makes the French quit league

indicators.note: to quit is to leave, so those letters go out of the word

blocks.note: the French word for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sickness forces French sides to withdraw from the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a fever with shivering fits, such as malaria.

clue.text: I play in Roman children's game

blocks.note: first meaning: the Latin verb for I play
second meaning: the board game with counters and a die

explanation.surface: A Roman child explaining what they are playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludo is the simple board game, and its name is Latin for I play.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a family board game where counters race round the board on dice throws.

clue.text: A warning to those who are too introspective?

definitions.text: to those who are too introspective

blocks.note: first meaning: a shout to beware of danger

blocks.clueFragment: to those who are too introspective
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: advice to people who only gaze inwards to turn their eyes the other way

explanation.surface: A caution addressed to people lost in their own thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: The warning cry is also literal advice to the introspective: stop looking in.
explanation.definitionFit: The shout is called out to alert someone to imminent danger, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: Not on green, perhaps, yet below par

blocks.note: first meaning: green is one example of a colour, so not on it is away from that colour
second meaning: slightly unwell

explanation.surface: A golfer who misses the green and finishes under par.
explanation.walkthrough: Green and par point to golf, but green is just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling off colour means being slightly ill, not at your usual healthy standard.

clue.text: Fair game?

blocks.note: first meaning: honourable, as in the phrase 'it's not ...' for unfair play
second meaning: the bat-and-ball sport

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' reads as a single phrase; split it. 'It's not cricket' is a British idiom for unsporting behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport is a byword for sportsmanship, hence the idiom using its name for fair conduct.

clue.text: Led a nun astray, but not charged

indicators.note: to go astray is to wander off course, so these letters stray into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone corrupted a nun yet escaped prosecution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not charged' suggests escaping the law, but it means carrying no load.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged can mean loaded, so an unladen lorry carries no cargo or burden.

clue.text: Full of zeal for a new trend

indicators.note: new signals a fresh form, so the letters after it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: An enthusiast keen on the latest fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and eager, burning with enthusiasm for a cause.

clue.text: Compositions one added to the performance

blocks.note: a concert is a musical performance
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pieces of music with one extra item put into the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerti is the Italian plural of concerto, a musical work for soloist and orchestra.

clue.text: Urges some simple modification

indicators.note: some modification means making changes to the word, so its letters are put in a new order
a modification is an alteration, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recommends making a few easy changes.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or push them forward, which is what urging does.

clue.text: Religious representation of two Greek letters

blocks.note: the first of the pair: the sixteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
the second of the pair: the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A sacred image made from a pair of Greek characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two Greek letters' supplies both pieces: PI and ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pieta is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ.

clue.text: Nerve twice required in traffic jam

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for courage
neck is slang for cheek or audacity

explanation.surface: It takes double courage to drive through a gridlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nerve twice' means two different words for nerve, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottleneck is a narrow point where traffic backs up, causing congestion and delay.

clue.text: Some currency back in circulation

blocks.note: surface reading: money returning to use
setter's reading: currency as the state of flowing, a current of water turning back in a circle

explanation.walkthrough: Currency suggests money, but it is the flow of a current; part of it swirls backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a whirling water movement running against the main stream in a circle.

clue.text: Hitherto the aim of boys wanting to go out with girls

definitions.text: the aim of boys wanting to go out with girls

blocks.note: first meaning: up until now

blocks.clueFragment: the aim of boys wanting to go out with girls
blocks.note: second meaning: their purpose is to take someone out romantically

explanation.surface: Up to now, lads have simply wanted girlfriends.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means so far or until the present, and also expresses purpose in courting.

clue.text: A race calling for tremendous effort

blocks.note: first meaning: a breed or stock of animals or plants
second meaning: a great exertion

explanation.surface: A contest demanding enormous exertion.
explanation.walkthrough: Race looks like a contest, but it means a breed or lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a variety or lineage within a species, and also a severe exertion.
